summary: Researched just after midnight on Mon 16 Nov and re-checked this morning with live prices; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the final check. It is the last Nations League matchday, so every game was checked first for a favourite with nothing left to play for. Eight games were researched: three are kept at medium, two at low and three are excluded. No favourite's price fell overnight. Medium: Iceland–Luxembourg (p 0.775; Iceland need a point for promotion, Luxembourg have lost four straight without scoring; Iceland lose Hordur (suspended), Stefan Teitur and Kristall Mani (injured), the forecast wind and sleet have eased), Lithuania–Liechtenstein (p 0.87; the coach reports a fit squad, Kucys suspended; Liechtenstein have not scored in the group), Slovenia at North Macedonia (p 0.62; Slovenia need the win for second place, North Macedonia are relegated with one goal in five games; Slovenia are without Bijol and Sesko). Low, so not bet: Greece–Serbia (Serbia's absentees and XI are now verified, but Greece have no probable XI after the 0-7 loss), Medvedev–Cobolli (no second bookmaker price; tennis now needs high anyway). Excluded: Switzerland–Scotland and Gibraltar–Malta (the favourite has already won its group and the opponent still needs the result; both prices fell 3–5%), Germany–Netherlands (fierce rivalry, near coin flip).

checks.team_news: Updated this morning: coach Mindaugas Cepas's eve-of-match press conference (LRT, 15 Nov) says all players are fit and ready, with no injuries or illness reported. Armandas Kucys is confirmed suspended; Cepas did not name the replacement and listed Faustas Steponavicius, Manfredas Ruzgis and Edgaras Dubickas as options, so the attack looks no stronger than expected. He said the three days between games were used to fix the problems seen against Suriname. Liechtenstein: nothing new found this morning; last night's report of a fully fit squad (GK Tim-Tiado Oehri back from an ACL injury, 19-year-old Yonas Abido's first call-up) still stands. Searches did not surface any Vaterland, Volksblatt or lfv.li report with news of absentees or a changed XI.
checks.lineups: Not out and no new expected XI found this morning. Cepas did not reveal his side. Sports Mole's predicted XI is unchanged (Lithuania Bartkus; Sirvys, Kazukolovas, Utkus, Lasickas; Gineitis, Vorobjovas, Michelbrink; Jankauskas, Dubickas, Venckus; Liechtenstein 5-4-1 type shape). Official XIs to be checked about 60 minutes before kick-off.
checks.rotation: Cepas described the 0-0 v Suriname on 12 Nov as a game with many chances but no goal and said the team must be calmer and more patient in the final third. That points to a settled side, not heavy rotation, though the XI is unconfirmed. Liechtenstein lost 0-1 to Azerbaijan on 13 Nov and travel after a 3-day turnaround.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Azerbaijan's win over Liechtenstein secured first place in the group. Cepas said Lithuania will not lack motivation and will make every effort to win; they need a point for 2nd place, and only a defeat would put it at risk. Liechtenstein have nothing realistic to play for beyond avoiding last place. League D is being abolished, so all teams move up to League C anyway. Interim coach Cepas has been in post 26 days, so the 7-day hard rule does not apply, and this is his second match. Not a derby.
checks.form: Lithuania: 2-0 at Liechtenstein, 1-1 v Azerbaijan, 0-1 at Azerbaijan, 0-0 v Suriname (many chances, none scored); only 3 goals in 3 group games. Liechtenstein: 0 goals in all three group games and in their last five matches, 1W 1D 13L in the last 15. Cepas himself describes them as physical and compact, defending in a low block and building through the middle, which fits a low-scoring game.
checks.h2h: Lithuania won 2-0 away on 24 Sep 2026, and the last three meetings were all 2-0 Lithuania wins. The pattern is low scoring: a deep Liechtenstein block and few big Lithuanian wins.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket (06:53 UTC): Lithuania 88.3%, draw 9.2%, Liechtenstein 2.5%. First listed 87.5 / 9.45 / 3.1, so Lithuania has firmed about 0.9 points since first listing. The 24h move is flat (0.885 to 0.885), so there is no story behind it and no team-news driver found. DraftKings via ESPN: 1.10 / 8.5 / 20 (de-vigged 84.4 / 10.9 / 4.6), opening 1.08 / 9 / 21, with a total line of 2.5. Live legs: Liechtenstein +2.5 at 59.5% (60.5% when first listed), Lithuania -1.5 at 65.5%, over 1.5 at 76.5%, under 3.5 at 70.5%, BTTS no at 78.5%. No Stake or Rainbet price seen.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Lithuania 1280 v Liechtenstein 882, expected score 0.946. Squawka projects 2-0 and Sports Mole 3-0, both Lithuania.
checks.venue_weather: Darius and Girenas Stadium, Kaunas, kick-off 19:00 local (17:00 UTC). Forecast cold at 1-7 C, cloudy with light rain possible and a strong wind. No extreme weather or pitch problem found, and the conditions would slightly lower the goal count.

games.reason: Nothing overnight changes last night's view. The Lithuania coach reports a fully fit squad, Kucys is confirmed out with the replacement unnamed, and no Liechtenstein absentees or changes were found, so there is no sign of a much stronger attack or a weakened Liechtenstein defence. The price has barely moved (Lithuania 88.3% live). Probabilities sit slightly below the market for the favourite because of the interim coach, a striker missing, only 3 goals in 3 group games and the 0-0 v Suriname, the deep Liechtenstein block and the cold, windy forecast. Views are kept only for legs that rest on Liechtenstein defending deep and Lithuania struggling to score big: under 3.5, BTTS no and Liechtenstein +2.5, which loses only if Lithuania win by 3 or more. The -1.5 handicap and over 1.5 stay without views because their likely failure is a 1-0 win or a draw. The +2.5 view is set a little under its live market price (58% v 59.5%).
games.main_risk: A cagey 1-0 win or a draw, which would sink the handicap -1.5 and over 1.5 legs and hurt the outright win. For the Liechtenstein +2.5 slip leg the risk is a Lithuania win by 3 or more: they had many chances against Suriname and Cepas wants to convert them, a 3-0 win has been predicted by Sports Mole, and Liechtenstein have lost 13 of their last 15. Lineups not confirmed, and the replacement for Kucys is unknown.

checks.team_news: Updated this morning. Iceland: Hordur Bjorgvin Magnusson is suspended (fotbolti.net, mbl.is 13 Nov). Stefan Teitur Thordarson is ruled out injured (fotbolti.net likely-XI piece, 15 Nov), which settles last night's open question. Kristall Mani Ingason left the Bulgaria game injured, was due to have a scan on Sunday, and Visir lists Saevar Atli Magnusson as his replacement in the squad. The scan result was not found. Fotbolti.net quotes him saying a cruciate ligament tear would be the worst news. Hjortur Hermannsson, Brynjar Ingi Bjarnason and Saevar Atli Magnusson were called up. Albert Gudmundsson, goalkeeper Elias Rafn Olafsson and Andri Fannar Baldursson remain out (Visir, per last night). Luxembourg: Omar Natami suspended, Dirk Carlson back (Sports Mole, per last night). No new Luxembourg news was found.
checks.lineups: Fotbolti.net (15 Nov) expects two changes from the 5-0 win at Bulgaria. Hjortur Hermannsson is predicted in central defence for the suspended Hordur, with Gudlaugur Victor Palsson as the alternative and Brynjar Ingi also called up. Another preview has Danil Leo Gretarsson moving to the right and Aron Einar Gunnarsson as a contender at centre-back. Fotbolti.net also has Arnor Sigurdsson likely to replace Kristall Mani, ahead of Jon Dagur Thorsteinsson. Stefan Teitur and Kristall Mani are therefore not expected to start, so the tips.gg XI that kept them is out of date. Sports Mole's predicted Luxembourg XI (4-1-4-1) is unchanged from last night. Nothing is official; the XIs come about 60 minutes before kick-off.
checks.rotation: Arnar Gunnlaugsson said on Sunday (Visir and fotbolti.net) that he wants to change as little as possible after the 5-0 win but is forced to make two changes, and that all the players in the squad could start. The changes come from the suspension and the injuries, not from choice. It is the last group game, so there is no later fixture to save players for. Luxembourg lost 0-1 at Estonia and no heavy rotation was reported for them. Depth at centre-back is thin.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Iceland lead the group on 11 points from 5 games. Visir says a loss would let Estonia take first place by beating Bulgaria. A win secures the group and promotion; a draw is likely enough. Winning the group also helps seeding for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Luxembourg cannot move up and are playing for pride. The favourite still needs a result, so this is not an exclusion.
checks.form: Unchanged. Iceland: 1-1 Estonia, 3-0 at Luxembourg, 3-0 Bulgaria, 0-0 at Estonia, 5-0 at Bulgaria, with one goal conceded in five games. Luxembourg: four straight defeats without scoring (0-3 Iceland, 0-1 Estonia, 0-2 Bulgaria, 0-1 Estonia) after a 2-1 win at Bulgaria. Both Iceland draws came against Estonia.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Iceland won 3-0 in Luxembourg on 29 Sept 2026. Luxembourg have only two wins against Iceland (3-1 in Sept 2023 is the other), and none away.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Iceland win is 0.7895 (draw 0.152, away 0.059). It was first listed at 0.7765, so the favourite is up 1.3 points, and 0.775 last night. DraftKings via ESPN now has Iceland 1.21, draw 6.00, Luxembourg 11.0, against 1.31/5.00/8.50 at the open (de-vigged 76.2/15.4/8.4, total 2.5). Last night it was 1.26/5.50/9.50. The move is small and runs in the favourite's favour. The team-news losses (Stefan Teitur, Kristall Mani, Hordur) were already public and did not move it. No stories were found against Iceland. Stake and Rainbet not seen.
checks.models: World Football Elo: Iceland 1632, Luxembourg 1359, expected score for Iceland 0.895 (draw counted as half). Consistent with a win chance in the mid to high 70s.
checks.venue_weather: Laugardalsvollur, Reykjavik, 17:00 UTC, home venue. Yr hourly table for today shows -4C at 17:00 rising to -2C at 19:00, a moderate 6 m/s easterly wind, no precipitation (no sleet or snow) and partly cloudy skies. This is calmer and drier than last night's forecasts of 11 m/s with rain and sleet. Fotbolti.net's groundsman says there is no frost in the pitch, it is covered and in fairly good condition, and the undersoil heating has been at maximum for weeks. Little risk to the match. The kick-off listing at 12:00 on one site is a conflict; everything else says 17:00 UTC.

games.reason: Iceland are clear favourites: Elo 1632 vs 1359, DraftKings 1.21 and a live Polymarket price of 78.9%. They are at home, need only a point for promotion, and face a bottom side that has lost four in a row without scoring. I sit slightly under the market (77.5% vs 78.9%) and keep the away chance at 6.5% because Iceland lose Stefan Teitur, Kristall Mani and the suspended Hordur, with centre-back depth thin. The draw is held at 16%, with Iceland's two draws against Estonia as the reason it stays real. The weather is now calmer than feared. A straight win is allowed since the draw is under 25%.
games.main_risk: A narrow home win or a draw: Iceland drew 0-0 and 1-1 with Estonia, and they now have a makeshift back line (Hjortur or Gudlaugur Victor at centre-back, Daniel Leo moved across) plus a weaker attack without Kristall Mani and Stefan Teitur. A Luxembourg side with nothing to lose could sit deep. Kristall Mani's scan result and the official XIs are still unknown.

checks.team_news: Neither is out. Cobolli (No.5 seed, Finals debut) retired in tears in Vienna R2 trailing Berrettini 5-2 in the 1st set; scans showed a minor left-leg muscle strain and he skipped the Paris Masters (tennismajors, flashscore). Per tennisworlditalia/tennisitaliano he says the injury is behind him and he trained at the Fan Village on Sunday with no visible problems, but I found no match played since the Vienna retirement. Medvedev (No.4 seed) had no injury reported; he said he was 'a bit tired' in Almaty in October. Sinner is out (knee), so the Finals field is not the original one. Alcaraz, the other group favourite, had a stomach issue and knee worries in practice. De Minaur and Fritz are alternates and nothing says either was called in.
checks.lineups: Order of play confirmed by Tennis Majors and tennistale: Mon 16 Nov, Inalpi Arena, Turin. Alcaraz v Tiafoe at 2pm CET; Medvedev v Cobolli is the night session, not before 8:30pm CET (19:30 UTC), matching the listed start. One search snippet claimed a Tuesday slot but the official order of play says Monday. No withdrawal or walkover announced.
checks.rotation: This is the first round-robin match for both. ATP group standings page shows all four Lendl Group players at no record yet. Medvedev's last event, the Paris Masters, ended with a 6-4 6-4 R2 loss to Buse on 4 Nov, so he has had about 11 days of rest. Cobolli has played nothing since the Vienna retirement (late Oct), so he comes in with match rust. Medvedev also played a heavy autumn: Almaty, Vienna, Paris. Next matches in the group are Alcaraz and Tiafoe.
checks.motivation: Group table before the game: all four 0-0 (Alcaraz, Medvedev, Cobolli, Tiafoe), so both players still have everything to play for. Top two go to the semi-finals, and a loss here leaves a player needing wins against Alcaraz and Tiafoe. No dead-rubber risk. Cobolli has the home crowd and high motivation in Turin.
checks.form: Medvedev: 3 titles this season and the most hard-court wins on tour (tennismajors, Oct). He went 11-1 in China, winning Hangzhou and reaching the Beijing SF, then lost the Shanghai SF to Jodar. He also played Almaty and Vienna, whose results I could not verify, then lost to Buse 6-4 6-4 in Paris R2 on 4 Nov. Cobolli: a strong season with a Roland Garros final run, qualifying for Turin for the first time; he beat Medvedev in Madrid in April, retired v Berrettini in Vienna, and withdrew from Paris. I could not retrieve a full last-10 list for either player (Tennis Abstract pages returned no data), so form is only partly verified.
checks.h2h: Medvedev leads 2-1 (tennismylife, ATP draw page). Medvedev won Beijing 2024 QF 6-2 6-4 (hard) and US Open 2024 R32 6-3 6-4 6-3 (hard). Cobolli won Madrid R16 on 29 Apr 2026 on clay, 6-3 5-7 6-4. Both Medvedev wins were on hard courts, the surface in Turin (indoor hard). Medvedev's baseline-counterpunching game suits fast indoor hard, while Cobolli's heavy forehand and movement make rallies physical.
checks.odds: The only second bookmaker price I found for this fixture is not for the Finals. Dimers and Oddschecker had Medvedev -120 / Cobolli +105 for the April Madrid match (Dimers sim 54.7/45.3), which is old and on clay. data.odds with DraftKings/ESPN is absent for this game, so I have no current second-bookmaker price. Polymarket 76% Medvedev; 24h move 0.765 to 0.760 (relative -0.7%), so there is no price drop to explain. De-vig not possible without a current second price.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo (data.rating, tennisabstract.com/reports/atp_elo_ratings.html): Medvedev 1989.4 (hard 1960.6) vs Cobolli 1872.5 (hard 1797.2). Win probability for Medvedev: 66.2% overall, 71.9% hard, 69.1% blended. The bookmaker-free model sits 7 points below the Polymarket 76%, so I lower p to 0.72.
checks.venue_weather: Inalpi Arena, Turin, indoor hard court, best-of-three tie-break sets, so no weather risk. The crowd is strongly pro-Cobolli (Italian, debut at home), and the pace is fast, which suits Medvedev. Cobolli's Elo is much weaker on hard than overall.

games.reason: Medvedev is the sensible favourite: higher Elo on hard (about 69-72%), 2-1 head-to-head with both wins on hard, and Cobolli returning from a muscle strain with no match since Vienna. But confidence is low because the brief requires a verified second bookmaker price and a verified recent form list, and I found neither: there is no current non-Polymarket price for this match and no last-10 results for either player. Medvedev also lost early in Paris and Cobolli beat him in April.
games.main_risk: Cobolli wins in front of a home crowd, since his minor leg strain may have healed (he says it is behind him) and he beat Medvedev most recently in Madrid; Medvedev is also coming off a flat Paris loss and a long autumn. Opening group match nerves and a short best-of-three make an upset more plausible. Missing second price and incomplete form data keep confidence at low.

checks.team_news: Updated this morning. Greece: Kourbelis is out (Sport24). Ioannidis is also absent (Gazzetta). Tzolis is available. Saliakas and Zafeiris were suspended for the Dutch game and are back. No other injuries were reported. Serbia: Zivkovic and Dragojevic are confirmed out for the red cards against Germany (B92, Mozzart, Novosti), and Dragojevic has been sent to the U21s. Vlahovic is confirmed out. Pavlovic, Terzic, Kostic and Stankovic were already out (Novosti). Milenkovic IS in this squad and is expected to start. Mitrovic is not named in either Serbian article I read, so his status is unverified. Greek press speaks of seven Serbian absentees, which I did not verify. Lukic and Maksimovic return from suspension. Paunovic is back on the bench. The 0-7 loss is confirmed by the Greek press.
checks.lineups: Serbia probable XI (Mozzart Sport): Petrovic; Erakovic, Milenkovic, Babic; Nedeljkovic, Maksimovic, Lukic, Bukinac; Samardzic, Jovic, S. Milinkovic-Savic. Greece: no probable XI. Gazzetta (Monday) names only candidates and expects changes from the Dutch XI (Tzolakis; Tsimikas, Retsos, Mavropanos, Rota; Androutsos, Triantis; Tzolis, Karetsas; Ioannidis, Pavlidis). Candidates are Saliakas, Chatzidiakos, Giannoulis, Zafeiris and Vagiannidis, and a switch to 4-2-3-1 is possible. Official XIs come about 60 minutes before the 21:45 Greek time (19:45 UTC) kick-off.
checks.rotation: Greece play three days after the 0-7 loss, and Gazzetta expects changes in defence, midfield and attack. Jovanovic said the team has the right pride to react and would not accept the favourite's role. Serbia are rested in midfield (Lukic and Maksimovic return) but lose Zivkovic and Dragojevic and have changes at the back (Erakovic in for Gudelj) and in goal (Petrovic).
checks.motivation: Table taken from last night (Netherlands 11, Germany 8, Greece 8, Serbia 0). I did not re-verify it this morning, and no article I read covered it or the Germany-Netherlands game at the same time. Greece still need a result. Serbia are on 0 points and say they play for pride (Paunovic). The stadium is sold out (about 23,000).
checks.form: Unchanged. Greece: W 2-1 at Serbia, W 1-0 vs Germany, D 2-2 and L 0-7 vs the Netherlands. Serbia: 0 points from 5.
checks.h2h: Greece 2-1 Serbia in Belgrade on 24 Sep 2026 (Douvikas 90+5).
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: Greece 68.3%, draw 19.3%, Serbia 12.4%. Greece were 67.3% when first listed, so the move is about +1 point. The 24h move is 67.5% to 68.5%. DraftKings is 1.42 / 4.50 / 6.50, opening 1.43, de-vig 65.2/20.5/14.2. The small drift towards Greece fits Serbia's suspensions and is not unexplained. My p is below the market on Greece because of the unconfirmed XI and the 0-7 hangover.
checks.models: Elo: Greece 1788, Serbia 1662, expected score 0.786. This is in line with the market.
checks.venue_weather: Panthessaliko Stadium, Volos, Greece's home ground. The Serbian press says it is sold out. No weather check.

games.reason: Fixture and kick-off confirmed (21:45 Greek time, 19:45 UTC). New this morning: Serbia's absentees and probable XI are verified, with Zivkovic, Dragojevic and Vlahovic out and Milenkovic playing. Greece have no probable XI yet, with only candidates and expected changes after the 0-7 loss. Mitrovic's status is not confirmed. Confidence stays low because the Greek XI is unknown and one Serbian absentee is unchecked. The market move since listing is small and explained.
games.main_risk: Greece's unknown XI after the 0-7 loss, which means rotation, morale and a leaky defence, so a draw or one-goal win is the main risk. Serbia have little to lose and have scored 4 in 5. Against that, Serbia's weakened squad and the sold-out home crowd favour Greece.

games.reason: Hard rule: the favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent still does. Group D1 is a three-team group. Sky Sports table (updated 15 Nov 21:48): Malta P3 W2 D1 L0 GF4 GA2 Pts7; Andorra P4 W1 D1 L2 GF3 GA3 Pts4 (finished); Gibraltar P3 W0 D2 L1 GF1 GA3 Pts2. This is the last match for Malta and Gibraltar (round 6). Malta (7 pts) cannot be caught, because Andorra max 4, so their group win is secured whatever happens. Gibraltar can still finish second above Andorra (a win gives 5 pts, a draw 3), so they still need a result and Malta do not. The Europa Point Stadium venue is Gibraltar's regular home ground, so it is not an exclusion reason. Malta's price also slid 66.5% to 64.5% (-3% relative) in 24h, and DraftKings moved from 1.43 to 1.49, with no news found to explain it. Lineups are not out, and no squad or injury news was found for either side. I could not confirm what second place is worth, but that does not change the dead-rubber verdict for the favourite.
games.main_risk: Malta already secured the group, so a rotated or unmotivated Malta side faces a Gibraltar side with something to gain. The first meeting finished 1-1, and the draw is priced at about 24%. Gibraltar have drawn 2 of their 3 games.

checks.team_news: Morning re-check, nothing new since last night. Slovenia: Jaka Bijol suspended (second yellow v Switzerland, RTV SLO, Planet Nogomet); Cesar's Sunday press conference gave no named replacement ('appropriate replacement' from the squad, decided at tactical training, Planet Nogomet); FotMob predicted XI lists Oblak in goal with Drkusic, Zec, Zaletel, Karnicnik in defence and Bijol unavailable (prediction only). Slovenia Oblak; Kuzmic, Drkusic, Bijol, Zaletel, Karnicnik; Matko, Zabukovnik, Cerin, Sturm; Vipotnik (stale, still lists Bijol). FotMob's version has Zec in the back line instead of Bijol. checks.rotation: No rotation risk found. Slovenia chase second place and Cesar asks maximum effort from starters and substitutes (Planet Nogomet). 3-day turnaround after Switzerland (0-0, 13 Nov); last matchday, so nothing after it to save players for. North Macedonia are relegated with no next fixture affecting this game. No new overnight story on squad changes.
checks.motivation: Group B1 before this game: Switzerland 13 pts (group won), Slovenia 8, Scotland 7, North Macedonia 0 (relegated to League C). Switzerland v Scotland is played the same day. A Slovenia win gives 11 pts, which Scotland (max 10) cannot match, so second place and the promotion play-off are secured. A draw (9 pts) is enough only if Scotland fail to beat Switzerland. Slovenia have everything to play for; North Macedonia play for pride and a first win. The dead-rubber rule does not apply.
checks.form: Slovenia Nations League: L W D W D (5 goals for, 3 against), last game 0-0 v Switzerland; conceded in all three away games. North Macedonia: 5 straight Nations League defeats, 1 goal scored and 12 conceded, no win in 13 games in all competitions. The small move is not tied to any news found (no new team-news story); it fits the steady drift toward the favourite. Draw no bet Slovenia live 87.7% (first listed 86.4%).
checks.models: World Football Elo: North Macedonia 1527, Slovenia 1726, expected score for the home side 0.361 (draw counts half), a smaller Slovenia edge than the market implies after the draw share. Statz had Slovenia 51% / North Macedonia 21%. Models are less bullish than the 64% market, so p is trimmed to 62% Slovenia.

games.reason: Slovenia are clear favourites (Elo 1726 v 1527, market 62-64%) and need the win to lock up second place; North Macedonia are relegated with 0 points and 1 goal in 5 games. This morning's re-check found no new negative news: Bijol still out with no confirmed replacement, Brekalo still doubtful, Oblak available, North Macedonia clean apart from Mitrovski's minor knock. The price moved slightly toward Slovenia without a visible news cause. The Slovenia draw-no-bet leg only loses if North Macedonia win (about 12-14% by market and book), and a draw is a push. Held at medium because Slovenia lack Bijol and Sesko, scored only 5 goals in 5 games, and the XI is unconfirmed.
games.main_risk: A North Macedonia win is the only way draw no bet loses, which needs a blunt Slovenia (no Sesko, a changed centre-back pairing without Bijol, possible Brekalo absence) to concede to a side that plans to attack more; a draw only voids the leg. For the other legs, a 0-0 or 1-1 or a one-goal Slovenia win hurts match-winner and handicap legs.

games.reason: Hard rule: the favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent still does. The ESPN Nations League standings, before this game, put Group B1 at: Switzerland P5 W4 D1 L0 GD +10, 13 pts; Slovenia P5 W2 D2 L1 GD +2, 8 pts; Scotland P5 W2 D1 L2 GD -1, 7 pts; North Macedonia P5 L5 GD -11, 0 pts. Switzerland can no longer be caught: Slovenia can reach 11 and Scotland 10, so Switzerland have already won the group and promotion to League A. Scotland are third, one point behind Slovenia. They still need a result to take second place and the promotion-playoff spot, so they have something to play for. The group's last matchday is on 16 Nov. Sources disagree on the exact table and on the playoff format. One preview lists Scotland on 4 pts, but the ESPN data matches Switzerland's 0-0 draw in Slovenia on 13 Nov and was used. I could not confirm whether second place or third place goes to the playoffs. Switzerland's 5.3% Polymarket price fall in 24h (0.565 to 0.535) and DraftKings' move from 1.67 to 1.77 also fit a side with nothing at stake. Another reason not to back Switzerland.
games.main_risk: Switzerland, already group winners and promoted, may rotate or ease off in a dead rubber, while Scotland need the result for the playoff spot. The Portugal 1-4 Denmark pattern applies.

games.reason: Hard rule: a fierce rivalry. Germany v Netherlands is one of international football's best-known rivalries, and the rules exclude derbies and fierce rivalries whatever the table says. It is also close to a coin flip: the market has Germany at about 50%, World Football Elo rates the Netherlands higher (1990 v 1916) and the first meeting this season finished 1-1.
